/**
 * CI check-run mirroring for dispatch-only workflows.
 *
 * Problem: when a repository's CI is triggered via workflow_dispatch
 * (no pull_request trigger), GitHub does not associate the run's check
 * runs with open PRs — the branch-protection required checks stay
 * "expected/pending" forever, and the real pass/fail is invisible in
 * the PR Checks tab (a zombie check-run may exist on the head SHA from
 * a stale push event).
 *
 * Fix: re-read the ACTUAL jobs of the dispatch run and re-create one
 * check-run per required check name on the PR head SHA (same names,
 * same conclusions, summary links back to the source run). GitHub's
 * Checks UI and branch protection take the LATEST check-run per
 * (name, head SHA), so the mirror overrides any zombie.
 *
 * Tools used (dmtools registry, snake_case, synchronous):
 *   github_get_workflow_run_jobs({workspace, repository, runId})
 *       -> { total_count, jobs: [{id, name, status, conclusion, html_url}] }
 *   github_create_check_run({workspace, repository, name, headSha
 *       [, status][, title][, summary][, text]})
 *       -> check-run object (use .id for the follow-up update)
 *   github_update_check_run({workspace, repository, checkRunId,
 *       status, conclusion[, title][, summary][, text]})
 *   github_create_commit_status({workspace, repository, sha, state
 *       [, description][, context][, targetUrl]})
 *
 * Conclusion policy (documented behaviour of stampRequiredChecks):
 *   - job.conclusion === 'skipped'         -> NOT stamped (a skipped job
 *       must never green a required check); recorded in `skipped`.
 *   - job.status !== 'completed' (running/queued/null conclusion)
 *                                          -> NOT stamped; `skipped`
 *       entry with reason 'not-completed'.
 *   - success | neutral                    -> stamped as 'success' (and
 *       commit-status 'success' when the fallback is on).
 *   - failure | timed_out | startup_failure | cancelled | action_required
 *                                          -> stamped as-is ('cancelled'
 *       and 'action_required' map to commit-status 'failure' — GitHub
 *       statuses have no neutral value, and a cancelled CI run must not
 *       read as green on a PR).
 *
 * Job matching: required check `name` is matched EXACTLY against the
 * job `name` (GitHub matrix jobs include the parenthesised variant, so
 * list the full name, e.g. "build (ubuntu-latest)"). When several jobs
 * share a name (re-runs, matrix), the LAST match in the run's job list
 * wins — it is the most recent attempt. A required entry may override
 * the matched job name with `jobName` when the protected check name
 * intentionally differs from the workflow job name.
 */

## PR Description

Closes #982
### What changed
`detectFailedChecks` now handles failed check-run `details_url`s shaped `/actions/runs/N` (no `/job/M` suffix): it resolves the run's failed jobs via `github_get_workflow_run_jobs` and fetches each failed job's log, so `ci_failures.md`/`ci_failures_full.log` are produced for those checks instead of being silently skipped.

### Key decisions
- `/runs/N/job/M` URLs keep the existing direct job-log path — the run-jobs lookup only runs when no job id is in the URL
- Added `getWorkflowRunJobs(runId)` to the GitHub SCM provider in `js/common/scm.js`; `githubHelpers` guards with `typeof === 'function'` so GitLab/ADO providers are unaffected (their `details_url` shapes don't match `/runs/N` anyway)
- Tolerates `{jobs: [...]}` / `{job_runs: [...]}` / bare-array run-jobs responses (mirrors `js/common/ci.js` `_jobsOf`)
- Only jobs concluding `failure`/`timed_out` get logs fetched (matches the check-level filter); per-job log sections are labelled with the job name

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_githubHelpers.json   # 76 passed
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json             # 3652 passed, 0 failed
```

<details><summary>Flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  CHECK[Failed check-run] --> URL{details_url shape?}
  URL -->|/runs/N/job/M| JOB[Direct github_get_job_logs]
  URL -->|/runs/N| RUN[github_get_workflow_run_jobs]
  RUN --> FILTER[Filter jobs: failure / timed_out]
  FILTER --> LOGS[get_job_logs per failed job]
  JOB --> MD[ci_failures.md + ci_failures_full.log]
  LOGS --> MD
```

</details>

/**
 * CI check-run mirroring for dispatch-only workflows.
 *
 * Problem: when a repository's CI is triggered via workflow_dispatch
 * (no pull_request trigger), GitHub does not associate the run's check
 * runs with open PRs — the branch-protection required checks stay
 * "expected/pending" forever, and the real pass/fail is invisible in
 * the PR Checks tab (a zombie check-run may exist on the head SHA from
 * a stale push event).
 *
 * Fix: re-read the ACTUAL jobs of the dispatch run and re-create one
 * check-run per required check name on the PR head SHA (same names,
 * same conclusions, summary links back to the source run). GitHub's
 * Checks UI and branch protection take the LATEST check-run per
 * (name, head SHA), so the mirror overrides any zombie.
 *
 * Tools used (dmtools registry, snake_case, synchronous):
 *   github_get_workflow_run_jobs({workspace, repository, runId})
 *       -> { total_count, jobs: [{id, name, status, conclusion, html_url}] }
 *   github_create_check_run({workspace, repository, name, headSha
 *       [, status][, title][, summary][, text]})
 *       -> check-run object (use .id for the follow-up update)
 *   github_update_check_run({workspace, repository, checkRunId,
 *       status, conclusion[, title][, summary][, text]})
 *   github_create_commit_status({workspace, repository, sha, state
 *       [, description][, context][, targetUrl]})
 *
 * Conclusion policy (documented behaviour of stampRequiredChecks):
 *   - job.conclusion === 'skipped'         -> NOT stamped (a skipped job
 *       must never green a required check); recorded in `skipped`.
 *   - job.status !== 'completed' (running/queued/null conclusion)
 *                                          -> NOT stamped; `skipped`
 *       entry with reason 'not-completed'.
 *   - success | neutral                    -> stamped as 'success' (and
 *       commit-status 'success' when the fallback is on).
 *   - failure | timed_out | startup_failure | cancelled | action_required
 *                                          -> stamped as-is ('cancelled'
 *       and 'action_required' map to commit-status 'failure' — GitHub
 *       statuses have no neutral value, and a cancelled CI run must not
 *       read as green on a PR).
 *
 * Job matching: required check `name` is matched EXACTLY against the
 * job `name` (GitHub matrix jobs include the parenthesised variant, so
 * list the full name, e.g. "build (ubuntu-latest)"). When several jobs
 * share a name (re-runs, matrix), the LAST match in the run's job list
 * wins — it is the most recent attempt. A required entry may override
 * the matched job name with `jobName` when the protected check name
 * intentionally differs from the workflow job name.
 */

}

38:- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) 3:# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
4:# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
5-# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
6-#
7-#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
8-#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
9-#   asset        crap-baseline.json
10-#
11-# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
12:#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
13:#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.

15-#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
16-#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
17-#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
18-#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 992
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/992
- **Title**: gh-982 smAgent detectFailedChecks misses /runs/N-shaped check-run URLs (context-prep half-b of the CI-failures blindness)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-982` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +327
- **Deletions**: -0
- **Created**: 2026-10-17T18:04:17Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-17T22:18:56Z

## PR Description

Closes #982
### What changed
`detectFailedChecks` now handles failed check-run `details_url`s shaped `/actions/runs/N` (no `/job/M` suffix): it resolves the run's failed jobs via `github_get_workflow_run_jobs` and fetches each failed job's log, so `ci_failures.md`/`ci_failures_full.log` are produced for those checks instead of being silently skipped.

### Key decisions
- `/runs/N/job/M` URLs keep the existing direct job-log path — the run-jobs lookup only runs when no job id is in the URL
- Added `getWorkflowRunJobs(runId)` to the GitHub SCM provider in `js/common/scm.js`; `githubHelpers` guards with `typeof === 'function'` so GitLab/ADO providers are unaffected (their `details_url` shapes don't match `/runs/N` anyway)
- Tolerates `{jobs: [...]}` / `{job_runs: [...]}` / bare-array run-jobs responses (mirrors `js/common/ci.js` `_jobsOf`)
- Only jobs concluding `failure`/`timed_out` get logs fetched (matches the check-level filter); per-job log sections are labelled with the job name

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_githubHelpers.json   # 76 passed
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json             # 3652 passed, 0 failed
```

<details><summary>Flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  CHECK[Failed check-run] --> URL{details_url shape?}
  URL -->|/runs/N/job/M| JOB[Direct github_get_job_logs]
  URL -->|/runs/N| RUN[github_get_workflow_run_jobs]
  RUN --> FILTER[Filter jobs: failure / timed_out]
  FILTER --> LOGS[get_job_logs per failed job]
  JOB --> MD[ci_failures.md + ci_failures_full.log]
  LOGS --> MD
```

</details>

/**
 * CI check-run mirroring for dispatch-only workflows.
 *
 * Problem: when a repository's CI is triggered via workflow_dispatch
 * (no pull_request trigger), GitHub does not associate the run's check
 * runs with open PRs — the branch-protection required checks stay
 * "expected/pending" forever, and the real pass/fail is invisible in
 * the PR Checks tab (a zombie check-run may exist on the head SHA from
 * a stale push event).
 *
 * Fix: re-read the ACTUAL jobs of the dispatch run and re-create one
 * check-run per required check name on the PR head SHA (same names,
 * same conclusions, summary links back to the source run). GitHub's
 * Checks UI and branch protection take the LATEST check-run per
 * (name, head SHA), so the mirror overrides any zombie.
 *
 * Tools used (dmtools registry, snake_case, synchronous):
 *   github_get_workflow_run_jobs({workspace, repository, runId})
 *       -> { total_count, jobs: [{id, name, status, conclusion, html_url}] }
 *   github_create_check_run({workspace, repository, name, headSha
 *       [, status][, title][, summary][, text]})
 *       -> check-run object (use .id for the follow-up update)
 *   github_update_check_run({workspace, repository, checkRunId,
 *       status, conclusion[, title][, summary][, text]})
 *   github_create_commit_status({workspace, repository, sha, state
 *       [, description][, context][, targetUrl]})
 *
 * Conclusion policy (documented behaviour of stampRequiredChecks):
 *   - job.conclusion === 'skipped'         -> NOT stamped (a skipped job
 *       must never green a required check); recorded in `skipped`.
 *   - job.status !== 'completed' (running/queued/null conclusion)
 *                                          -> NOT stamped; `skipped`
 *       entry with reason 'not-completed'.
 *   - success | neutral                    -> stamped as 'success' (and
 *       commit-status 'success' when the fallback is on).
 *   - failure | timed_out | startup_failure | cancelled | action_required
 *                                          -> stamped as-is ('cancelled'
 *       and 'action_required' map to commit-status 'failure' — GitHub
 *       statuses have no neutral value, and a cancelled CI run must not
 *       read as green on a PR).
 *
 * Job matching: required check `name` is matched EXACTLY against the
 * job `name` (GitHub matrix jobs include the parenthesised variant, so
 * list the full name, e.g. "build (ubuntu-latest)"). When several jobs
 * share a name (re-runs, matrix), the LAST match in the run's job list
 * wins — it is the most recent attempt. A required entry may override
 * the matched job name with `jobName` when the protected check name
 * intentionally differs from the workflow job name.
 */

## PR Description

Closes #982
### What changed
`detectFailedChecks` now handles failed check-run `details_url`s shaped `/actions/runs/N` (no `/job/M` suffix): it resolves the run's failed jobs via `github_get_workflow_run_jobs` and fetches each failed job's log, so `ci_failures.md`/`ci_failures_full.log` are produced for those checks instead of being silently skipped.

### Key decisions
- `/runs/N/job/M` URLs keep the existing direct job-log path — the run-jobs lookup only runs when no job id is in the URL
- Added `getWorkflowRunJobs(runId)` to the GitHub SCM provider in `js/common/scm.js`; `githubHelpers` guards with `typeof === 'function'` so GitLab/ADO providers are unaffected (their `details_url` shapes don't match `/runs/N` anyway)
- Tolerates `{jobs: [...]}` / `{job_runs: [...]}` / bare-array run-jobs responses (mirrors `js/common/ci.js` `_jobsOf`)
- Only jobs concluding `failure`/`timed_out` get logs fetched (matches the check-level filter); per-job log sections are labelled with the job name

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_githubHelpers.json   # 76 passed
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json             # 3652 passed, 0 failed
```

  CHECK[Failed check-run] --> URL{details_url shape?}

```

</details>

/**
 * CI check-run mirroring for dispatch-only workflows.
 *
 * Problem: when a repository's CI is triggered via workflow_dispatch
 * (no pull_request trigger), GitHub does not associate the run's check
 * runs with open PRs — the branch-protection required checks stay
 * "expected/pending" forever, and the real pass/fail is invisible in
 * the PR Checks tab (a zombie check-run may exist on the head SHA from
 * a stale push event).
 *
 * Fix: re-read the ACTUAL jobs of the dispatch run and re-create one
 * check-run per required check name on the PR head SHA (same names,
 * same conclusions, summary links back to the source run). GitHub's
 * Checks UI and branch protection take the LATEST check-run per
 * (name, head SHA), so the mirror overrides any zombie.
 *
 * Tools used (dmtools registry, snake_case, synchronous):
 *   github_get_workflow_run_jobs({workspace, repository, runId})
 *       -> { total_count, jobs: [{id, name, status, conclusion, html_url}] }
 *   github_create_check_run({workspace, repository, name, headSha
 *       [, status][, title][, summary][, text]})
 *       -> check-run object (use .id for the follow-up update)
 *   github_update_check_run({workspace, repository, checkRunId,
 *       status, conclusion[, title][, summary][, text]})
 *   github_create_commit_status({workspace, repository, sha, state
 *       [, description][, context][, targetUrl]})
 *
 * Conclusion policy (documented behaviour of stampRequiredChecks):
 *   - job.conclusion === 'skipped'         -> NOT stamped (a skipped job
 *       must never green a required check); recorded in `skipped`.
 *   - job.status !== 'completed' (running/queued/null conclusion)
 *                                          -> NOT stamped; `skipped`
 *       entry with reason 'not-completed'.
 *   - success | neutral                    -> stamped as 'success' (and
 *       commit-status 'success' when the fallback is on).
 *   - failure | timed_out | startup_failure | cancelled | action_required
 *                                          -> stamped as-is ('cancelled'
 *       and 'action_required' map to commit-status 'failure' — GitHub
 *       statuses have no neutral value, and a cancelled CI run must not
 *       read as green on a PR).
 *
 * Job matching: required check `name` is matched EXACTLY against the
 * job `name` (GitHub matrix jobs include the parenthesised variant, so
 * list the full name, e.g. "build (ubuntu-latest)"). When several jobs
 * share a name (re-runs, matrix), the LAST match in the run's job list
 * wins — it is the most recent attempt. A required entry may override
 * the matched job name with `jobName` when the protected check name
 * intentionally differs from the workflow job name.
 */

## PR Description

Closes #982
### What changed
`detectFailedChecks` now handles failed check-run `details_url`s shaped `/actions/runs/N` (no `/job/M` suffix): it resolves the run's failed jobs via `github_get_workflow_run_jobs` and fetches each failed job's log, so `ci_failures.md`/`ci_failures_full.log` are produced for those checks instead of being silently skipped.

### Key decisions
- `/runs/N/job/M` URLs keep the existing direct job-log path — the run-jobs lookup only runs when no job id is in the URL
- Added `getWorkflowRunJobs(runId)` to the GitHub SCM provider in `js/common/scm.js`; `githubHelpers` guards with `typeof === 'function'` so GitLab/ADO providers are unaffected (their `details_url` shapes don't match `/runs/N` anyway)
- Tolerates `{jobs: [...]}` / `{job_runs: [...]}` / bare-array run-jobs responses (mirrors `js/common/ci.js` `_jobsOf`)
- Only jobs concluding `failure`/`timed_out` get logs fetched (matches the check-level filter); per-job log sections are labelled with the job name

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_githubHelpers.json   # 76 passed
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json             # 3652 passed, 0 failed
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  CHECK[Failed check-run] --> URL{details_url shape?}
  URL -->|/runs/N/job/M| JOB[Direct github_get_job_logs]
  URL -->|/runs/N| RUN[github_get_workflow_run_jobs]
  RUN --> FILTER[Filter jobs: failure / timed_out]
  FILTER --> LOGS[get_job_logs per failed job]
  JOB --> MD[ci_failures.md + ci_failures_full.log]
  LOGS --> MD
```

</details>

/**
 * CI check-run mirroring for dispatch-only workflows.
 *
 * Problem: when a repository's CI is triggered via workflow_dispatch
 * (no pull_request trigger), GitHub does not associate the run's check
 * runs with open PRs — the branch-protection required checks stay
 * "expected/pending" forever, and the real pass/fail is invisible in
 * the PR Checks tab (a zombie check-run may exist on the head SHA from
 * a stale push event).
 *
 * Fix: re-read the ACTUAL jobs of the dispatch run and re-create one
 * check-run per required check name on the PR head SHA (same names,
 * same conclusions, summary links back to the source run). GitHub's
 * Checks UI and branch protection take the LATEST check-run per
 * (name, head SHA), so the mirror overrides any zombie.
 *
 * Tools used (dmtools registry, snake_case, synchronous):
 *   github_get_workflow_run_jobs({workspace, repository, runId})
 *       -> { total_count, jobs: [{id, name, status, conclusion, html_url}] }
 *   github_create_check_run({workspace, repository, name, headSha
 *       [, status][, title][, summary][, text]})
 *       -> check-run object (use .id for the follow-up update)
 *   github_update_check_run({workspace, repository, checkRunId,
 *       status, conclusion[, title][, summary][, text]})
 *   github_create_commit_status({workspace, repository, sha, state
 *       [, description][, context][, targetUrl]})
 *
 * Conclusion policy (documented behaviour of stampRequiredChecks):
 *   - job.conclusion === 'skipped'         -> NOT stamped (a skipped job
 *       must never green a required check); recorded in `skipped`.
 *   - job.status !== 'completed' (running/queued/null conclusion)
 *                                          -> NOT stamped; `skipped`
 *       entry with reason 'not-completed'.
 *   - success | neutral                    -> stamped as 'success' (and
 *       commit-status 'success' when the fallback is on).
 *   - failure | timed_out | startup_failure | cancelled | action_required
 *                                          -> stamped as-is ('cancelled'
 *       and 'action_required' map to commit-status 'failure' — GitHub
 *       statuses have no neutral value, and a cancelled CI run must not
 *       read as green on a PR).
 *
 * Job matching: required check `name` is matched EXACTLY against the
 * job `name` (GitHub matrix jobs include the parenthesised variant, so
 * list the full name, e.g. "build (ubuntu-latest)"). When several jobs
 * share a name (re-runs, matrix), the LAST match in the run's job list
 * wins — it is the most recent attempt. A required entry may override
 * the matched job name with `jobName` when the protected check name
 * intentionally differs from the workflow job name.
 */

1:# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
2-#
3:# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
4:# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
5-# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
6-#
7-#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
8-#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
9-#   asset        crap-baseline.json
10-#
11-# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
12:#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
13:#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
14-# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
15-#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
16-#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
17-#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
18-#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
--
49-  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
50-  cancel-in-progress: false
51-
52-env:
53-  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
54:  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
55:  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
56:  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
57-  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
58-  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'
59-
60-jobs:
61-  gate:
--
100-          node-version: 20
101-
102-      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
103-        run: |
104-          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
105:            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17
106-
107-      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
108-        run: |
109-          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
110-            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
--
149-        run: |
150-          set +e
151-          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
152-          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
153-            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
154:            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
155-            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
156-          code=$?
157-          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
158:          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
159-          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
160-          exit $code
161-
162-      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
163-        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 992
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/992
- **Title**: gh-982 smAgent detectFailedChecks misses /runs/N-shaped check-run URLs (context-prep half-b of the CI-failures blindness)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-982` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +327
- **Deletions**: -0
- **Created**: 2026-10-17T18:04:17Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-17T22:18:56Z

## PR Description

Closes #982
### What changed
`detectFailedChecks` now handles failed check-run `details_url`s shaped `/actions/runs/N` (no `/job/M` suffix): it resolves the run's failed jobs via `github_get_workflow_run_jobs` and fetches each failed job's log, so `ci_failures.md`/`ci_failures_full.log` are produced for those checks instead of being silently skipped.

### Key decisions
- `/runs/N/job/M` URLs keep the existing direct job-log path — the run-jobs lookup only runs when no job id is in the URL
- Added `getWorkflowRunJobs(runId)` to the GitHub SCM provider in `js/common/scm.js`; `githubHelpers` guards with `typeof === 'function'` so GitLab/ADO providers are unaffected (their `details_url` shapes don't match `/runs/N` anyway)
- Tolerates `{jobs: [...]}` / `{job_runs: [...]}` / bare-array run-jobs responses (mirrors `js/common/ci.js` `_jobsOf`)
- Only jobs concluding `failure`/`timed_out` get logs fetched (matches the check-level filter); per-job log sections are labelled with the job name

### How to verify

/**
 * CI check-run mirroring for dispatch-only workflows.
 *
 * Problem: when a repository's CI is triggered via workflow_dispatch
 * (no pull_request trigger), GitHub does not associate the run's check
 * runs with open PRs — the branch-protection required checks stay
 * "expected/pending" forever, and the real pass/fail is invisible in
 * the PR Checks tab (a zombie check-run may exist on the head SHA from
 * a stale push event).
 *
 * Fix: re-read the ACTUAL jobs of the dispatch run and re-create one
 * check-run per required check name on the PR head SHA (same names,
 * same conclusions, summary links back to the source run). GitHub's
 * Checks UI and branch protection take the LATEST check-run per
 * (name, head SHA), so the mirror overrides any zombie.
 *
 * Tools used (dmtools registry, snake_case, synchronous):
 *   github_get_workflow_run_jobs({workspace, repository, runId})
 *       -> { total_count, jobs: [{id, name, status, conclusion, html_url}] }
 *   github_create_check_run({workspace, repository, name, headSha
 *       [, status][, title][, summary][, text]})
 *       -> check-run object (use .id for the follow-up update)
 *   github_update_check_run({workspace, repository, checkRunId,
 *       status, conclusion[, title][, summary][, text]})
 *   github_create_commit_status({workspace, repository, sha, state
 *       [, description][, context][, targetUrl]})
 *
 * Conclusion policy (documented behaviour of stampRequiredChecks):
 *   - job.conclusion === 'skipped'         -> NOT stamped (a skipped job
 *       must never green a required check); recorded in `skipped`.
 *   - job.status !== 'completed' (running/queued/null conclusion)
 *                                          -> NOT stamped; `skipped`
 *       entry with reason 'not-completed'.
 *   - success | neutral                    -> stamped as 'success' (and
 *       commit-status 'success' when the fallback is on).
 *   - failure | timed_out | startup_failure | cancelled | action_required
 *                                          -> stamped as-is ('cancelled'
 *       and 'action_required' map to commit-status 'failure' — GitHub
 *       statuses have no neutral value, and a cancelled CI run must not
 *       read as green on a PR).
 *
 * Job matching: required check `name` is matched EXACTLY against the
 * job `name` (GitHub matrix jobs include the parenthesised variant, so
 * list the full name, e.g. "build (ubuntu-latest)"). When several jobs
 * share a name (re-runs, matrix), the LAST match in the run's job list
 * wins — it is the most recent attempt. A required entry may override
 * the matched job name with `jobName` when the protected check name
 * intentionally differs from the workflow job name.
 */

- **PR #**: 992

- **Title**: gh-982 smAgent detectFailedChecks misses /runs/N-shaped check-run URLs (context-prep half-b of the CI-failures blindness)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-982` → `main`

- **Updated**: 2026-10-17T22:18:56Z

## PR Description

Closes #982
### What changed
`detectFailedChecks` now handles failed check-run `details_url`s shaped `/actions/runs/N` (no `/job/M` suffix): it resolves the run's failed jobs via `github_get_workflow_run_jobs` and fetches each failed job's log, so `ci_failures.md`/`ci_failures_full.log` are produced for those checks instead of being silently skipped.

### Key decisions
- `/runs/N/job/M` URLs keep the existing direct job-log path — the run-jobs lookup only runs when no job id is in the URL
- Added `getWorkflowRunJobs(runId)` to the GitHub SCM provider in `js/common/scm.js`; `githubHelpers` guards with `typeof === 'function'` so GitLab/ADO providers are unaffected (their `details_url` shapes don't match `/runs/N` anyway)
- Tolerates `{jobs: [...]}` / `{job_runs: [...]}` / bare-array run-jobs responses (mirrors `js/common/ci.js` `_jobsOf`)
- Only jobs concluding `failure`/`timed_out` get logs fetched (matches the check-level filter); per-job log sections are labelled with the job name

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_githubHelpers.json   # 76 passed
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json             # 3652 passed, 0 failed
```

<details><summary>Flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  CHECK[Failed check-run] --> URL{details_url shape?}
  URL -->|/runs/N/job/M| JOB[Direct github_get_job_logs]
  URL -->|/runs/N| RUN[github_get_workflow_run_jobs]
  RUN --> FILTER[Filter jobs: failure / timed_out]
  FILTER --> LOGS[get_job_logs per failed job]
  JOB --> MD[ci_failures.md + ci_failures_full.log]
  LOGS --> MD
```

</details>

/**
 * CI check-run mirroring for dispatch-only workflows.
 *
 * Problem: when a repository's CI is triggered via workflow_dispatch
 * (no pull_request trigger), GitHub does not associate the run's check
 * runs with open PRs — the branch-protection required checks stay
 * "expected/pending" forever, and the real pass/fail is invisible in
 * the PR Checks tab (a zombie check-run may exist on the head SHA from
 * a stale push event).
 *
 * Fix: re-read the ACTUAL jobs of the dispatch run and re-create one
 * check-run per required check name on the PR head SHA (same names,
 * same conclusions, summary links back to the source run). GitHub's
 * Checks UI and branch protection take the LATEST check-run per
 * (name, head SHA), so the mirror overrides any zombie.
 *
 * Tools used (dmtools registry, snake_case, synchronous):
 *   github_get_workflow_run_jobs({workspace, repository, runId})
 *       -> { total_count, jobs: [{id, name, status, conclusion, html_url}] }
 *   github_create_check_run({workspace, repository, name, headSha
 *       [, status][, title][, summary][, text]})
 *       -> check-run object (use .id for the follow-up update)
 *   github_update_check_run({workspace, repository, checkRunId,
 *       status, conclusion[, title][, summary][, text]})
 *   github_create_commit_status({workspace, repository, sha, state
 *       [, description][, context][, targetUrl]})
 *
 * Conclusion policy (documented behaviour of stampRequiredChecks):
 *   - job.conclusion === 'skipped'         -> NOT stamped (a skipped job
 *       must never green a required check); recorded in `skipped`.
 *   - job.status !== 'completed' (running/queued/null conclusion)
 *                                          -> NOT stamped; `skipped`
 *       entry with reason 'not-completed'.
 *   - success | neutral                    -> stamped as 'success' (and
 *       commit-status 'success' when the fallback is on).
 *   - failure | timed_out | startup_failure | cancelled | action_required
 *                                          -> stamped as-is ('cancelled'
 *       and 'action_required' map to commit-status 'failure' — GitHub
 *       statuses have no neutral value, and a cancelled CI run must not
 *       read as green on a PR).
 *
 * Job matching: required check `name` is matched EXACTLY against the
 * job `name` (GitHub matrix jobs include the parenthesised variant, so
 * list the full name, e.g. "build (ubuntu-latest)"). When several jobs
 * share a name (re-runs, matrix), the LAST match in the run's job list
 * wins — it is the most recent attempt. A required entry may override
 * the matched job name with `jobName` when the protected check name
 * intentionally differs from the workflow job name.
 */

function _parseJson(raw) {
    if (typeof raw === 'string') {
        try { return JSON.parse(raw); } catch (e) { return raw; }
    }
    return raw;
}

function _jobsOf(response) {
    var parsed = _parseJson(response);
    if (parsed && Array.isArray(parsed.jobs)) return parsed.jobs;

4:# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
5-# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
6-#
7-#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
8-#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)

# pr-992: gh-982 smAgent detectFailedChecks misses /runs/N-shaped check-run URLs (context-prep half-b of the CI-failures blindness)

## Description

Closes #982
### What changed
`detectFailedChecks` now handles failed check-run `details_url`s shaped `/actions/runs/N` (no `/job/M` suffix): it resolves the run's failed jobs via `github_get_workflow_run_jobs` and fetches each failed job's log, so `ci_failures.md`/`ci_failures_full.log` are produced for those checks instead of being silently skipped.

### Key decisions
- `/runs/N/job/M` URLs keep the existing direct job-log path — the run-jobs lookup only runs when no job id is in the URL
- Added `getWorkflowRunJobs(runId)` to the GitHub SCM provider in `js/common/scm.js`; `githubHelpers` guards with `typeof === 'function'` so GitLab/ADO providers are unaffected (their `details_url` shapes don't match `/runs/N` anyway)
- Tolerates `{jobs: [...]}` / `{job_runs: [...]}` / bare-array run-jobs responses (mirrors `js/common/ci.js` `_jobsOf`)
- Only jobs concluding `failure`/`timed_out` get logs fetched (matches the check-level filter); per-job log sections are labelled with the job name

### How to verify
```bash

blocks.text:
/**
 * CI check-run mirroring for dispatch-only workflows.
 *
 * Problem: when a repository's CI is triggered via workflow_dispatch
 * (no pull_request trigger), GitHub does not associate the run's check
 * runs with open PRs — the branch-protection required checks stay
 * "expected/pending" forever, and the real pass/fail is invisible in
 * the PR Checks tab (a zombie check-run may exist on the head SHA from
 * a stale push event).
 *
 * Fix: re-read the ACTUAL jobs of the dispatch run and re-create one
 * check-run per required check name on the PR head SHA (same names,
 * same conclusions, summary links back to the source run). GitHub's
 * Checks UI and branch protection take the LATEST check-run per
 * (name, head SHA), so the mirror overrides any zombie.
 *
 * Tools used (dmtools registry, snake_case, synchronous):
 *   github_get_workflow_run_jobs({workspace, repository, runId})
 *       -> { total_count, jobs: [{id, name, status, conclusion, html_url}] }
 *   github_create_check_run({workspace, repository, name, headSha
 *       [, status][, title][, summary][, text]})
 *       -> check-run object (use .id for the follow-up update)
 *   github_update_check_run({workspace, repository, checkRunId,
 *       status, conclusion[, title][, summary][, text]})
 *   github_create_commit_status({workspace, repository, sha, state
 *       [, description][, context][, targetUrl]})
 *
 * Conclusion policy (documented behaviour of stampRequiredChecks):
 *   - job.conclusion === 'skipped'         -> NOT stamped (a skipped job
 *       must never green a required check); recorded in `skipped`.
 *   - job.status !== 'completed' (running/queued/null conclusion)
 *                                          -> NOT stamped; `skipped`
 *       entry with reason 'not-completed'.
 *   - success | neutral                    -> stamped as 'success' (and
 *       commit-status 'success' when the fallback is on).
 *   - failure | timed_out | startup_failure | cancelled | action_required
 *                                          -> stamped as-is ('cancelled'
 *       and 'action_required' map to commit-status 'failure' — GitHub
 *       statuses have no neutral value, and a cancelled CI run must not
 *       read as green on a PR).
 *
 * Job matching: required check `name` is matched EXACTLY against the
 * job `name` (GitHub matrix jobs include the parenthesised variant, so
 * list the full name, e.g. "build (ubuntu-latest)"). When several jobs
 * share a name (re-runs, matrix), the LAST match in the run's job list
 * wins — it is the most recent attempt. A required entry may override
 * the matched job name with `jobName` when the protected check name
 * intentionally differs from the workflow job name.
 */

38:- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.

1:# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
2-#
3:# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
4:# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
5-# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
6-#
7-#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
8-#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
9-#   asset        crap-baseline.json
10-#
11-# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
12:#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
13:#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
14-# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
15-#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
16-#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
17-#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
18-#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.

# pr-992: gh-982 smAgent detectFailedChecks misses /runs/N-shaped check-run URLs (context-prep half-b of the CI-failures blindness)

## Description

Closes #982
### What changed
`detectFailedChecks` now handles failed check-run `details_url`s shaped `/actions/runs/N` (no `/job/M` suffix): it resolves the run's failed jobs via `github_get_workflow_run_jobs` and fetches each failed job's log, so `ci_failures.md`/`ci_failures_full.log` are produced for those checks instead of being silently skipped.

### Key decisions
- `/runs/N/job/M` URLs keep the existing direct job-log path — the run-jobs lookup only runs when no job id is in the URL
- Added `getWorkflowRunJobs(runId)` to the GitHub SCM provider in `js/common/scm.js`; `githubHelpers` guards with `typeof === 'function'` so GitLab/ADO providers are unaffected (their `details_url` shapes don't match `/runs/N` anyway)
- Tolerates `{jobs: [...]}` / `{job_runs: [...]}` / bare-array run-jobs responses (mirrors `js/common/ci.js` `_jobsOf`)
- Only jobs concluding `failure`/`timed_out` get logs fetched (matches the check-level filter); per-job log sections are labelled with the job name

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_githubHelpers.json   # 76 passed
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json             # 3652 passed, 0 failed
```

<details><summary>Flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  CHECK[Failed check-run] --> URL{details_url shape?}
  URL -->|/runs/N/job/M| JOB[Direct github_get_job_logs]
  URL -->|/runs/N| RUN[github_get_workflow_run_jobs]
  RUN --> FILTER[Filter jobs: failure / timed_out]
  FILTER --> LOGS[get_job_logs per failed job]
  JOB --> MD[ci_failures.md + ci_failures_full.log]
  LOGS --> MD
```

</details>

/**
 * CI check-run mirroring for dispatch-only workflows.
 *
 * Problem: when a repository's CI is triggered via workflow_dispatch
 * (no pull_request trigger), GitHub does not associate the run's check
 * runs with open PRs — the branch-protection required checks stay
 * "expected/pending" forever, and the real pass/fail is invisible in
 * the PR Checks tab (a zombie check-run may exist on the head SHA from
 * a stale push event).
 *
 * Fix: re-read the ACTUAL jobs of the dispatch run and re-create one
 * check-run per required check name on the PR head SHA (same names,
 * same conclusions, summary links back to the source run). GitHub's
 * Checks UI and branch protection take the LATEST check-run per
 * (name, head SHA), so the mirror overrides any zombie.
 *
 * Tools used (dmtools registry, snake_case, synchronous):
 *   github_get_workflow_run_jobs({workspace, repository, runId})
 *       -> { total_count, jobs: [{id, name, status, conclusion, html_url}] }
 *   github_create_check_run({workspace, repository, name, headSha
 *       [, status][, title][, summary][, text]})
 *       -> check-run object (use .id for the follow-up update)
 *   github_update_check_run({workspace, repository, checkRunId,
 *       status, conclusion[, title][, summary][, text]})
 *   github_create_commit_status({workspace, repository, sha, state
 *       [, description][, context][, targetUrl]})
 *
 * Conclusion policy (documented behaviour of stampRequiredChecks):
 *   - job.conclusion === 'skipped'         -> NOT stamped (a skipped job
 *       must never green a required check); recorded in `skipped`.
 *   - job.status !== 'completed' (running/queued/null conclusion)
 *                                          -> NOT stamped; `skipped`
 *       entry with reason 'not-completed'.
 *   - success | neutral                    -> stamped as 'success' (and
 *       commit-status 'success' when the fallback is on).
 *   - failure | timed_out | startup_failure | cancelled | action_required
 *                                          -> stamped as-is ('cancelled'
 *       and 'action_required' map to commit-status 'failure' — GitHub
 *       statuses have no neutral value, and a cancelled CI run must not
 *       read as green on a PR).
 *
 * Job matching: required check `name` is matched EXACTLY against the
 * job `name` (GitHub matrix jobs include the parenthesised variant, so
 * list the full name, e.g. "build (ubuntu-latest)"). When several jobs
 * share a name (re-runs, matrix), the LAST match in the run's job list
 * wins — it is the most recent attempt. A required entry may override
 * the matched job name with `jobName` when the protected check name
 * intentionally differs from the workflow job name.
 */

}

# pr-992: gh-982 smAgent detectFailedChecks misses /runs/N-shaped check-run URLs (context-prep half-b of the CI-failures blindness)

## Description

Closes #982
### What changed
`detectFailedChecks` now handles failed check-run `details_url`s shaped `/actions/runs/N` (no `/job/M` suffix): it resolves the run's failed jobs via `github_get_workflow_run_jobs` and fetches each failed job's log, so `ci_failures.md`/`ci_failures_full.log` are produced for those checks instead of being silently skipped.

### Key decisions
- `/runs/N/job/M` URLs keep the existing direct job-log path — the run-jobs lookup only runs when no job id is in the URL
- Added `getWorkflowRunJobs(runId)` to the GitHub SCM provider in `js/common/scm.js`; `githubHelpers` guards with `typeof === 'function'` so GitLab/ADO providers are unaffected (their `details_url` shapes don't match `/runs/N` anyway)
- Tolerates `{jobs: [...]}` / `{job_runs: [...]}` / bare-array run-jobs responses (mirrors `js/common/ci.js` `_jobsOf`)
- Only jobs concluding `failure`/`timed_out` get logs fetched (matches the check-level filter); per-job log sections are labelled with the job name

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_githubHelpers.json   # 76 passed
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json             # 3652 passed, 0 failed
```

<details><summary>Flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  CHECK[Failed check-run] --> URL{details_url shape?}
  URL -->|/runs/N/job/M| JOB[Direct github_get_job_logs]
  URL -->|/runs/N| RUN[github_get_workflow_run_jobs]
  RUN --> FILTER[Filter jobs: failure / timed_out]
  FILTER --> LOGS[get_job_logs per failed job]
  JOB --> MD[ci_failures.md + ci_failures_full.log]
  LOGS --> MD
```

</details>

/**
 * CI check-run mirroring for dispatch-only workflows.
 *
 * Problem: when a repository's CI is triggered via workflow_dispatch
 * (no pull_request trigger), GitHub does not associate the run's check
 * runs with open PRs — the branch-protection required checks stay
 * "expected/pending" forever, and the real pass/fail is invisible in
 * the PR Checks tab (a zombie check-run may exist on the head SHA from
 * a stale push event).
 *
 * Fix: re-read the ACTUAL jobs of the dispatch run and re-create one
 * check-run per required check name on the PR head SHA (same names,
 * same conclusions, summary links back to the source run). GitHub's
 * Checks UI and branch protection take the LATEST check-run per
 * (name, head SHA), so the mirror overrides any zombie.
 *
 * Tools used (dmtools registry, snake_case, synchronous):
 *   github_get_workflow_run_jobs({workspace, repository, runId})
 *       -> { total_count, jobs: [{id, name, status, conclusion, html_url}] }
 *   github_create_check_run({workspace, repository, name, headSha
 *       [, status][, title][, summary][, text]})
 *       -> check-run object (use .id for the follow-up update)
 *   github_update_check_run({workspace, repository, checkRunId,
 *       status, conclusion[, title][, summary][, text]})
 *   github_create_commit_status({workspace, repository, sha, state
 *       [, description][, context][, targetUrl]})
 *
 * Conclusion policy (documented behaviour of stampRequiredChecks):
 *   - job.conclusion === 'skipped'         -> NOT stamped (a skipped job
 *       must never green a required check); recorded in `skipped`.
 *   - job.status !== 'completed' (running/queued/null conclusion)
 *                                          -> NOT stamped; `skipped`
 *       entry with reason 'not-completed'.
 *   - success | neutral                    -> stamped as 'success' (and
 *       commit-status 'success' when the fallback is on).
 *   - failure | timed_out | startup_failure | cancelled | action_required
 *                                          -> stamped as-is ('cancelled'
 *       and 'action_required' map to commit-status 'failure' — GitHub
 *       statuses have no neutral value, and a cancelled CI run must not
 *       read as green on a PR).
 *
 * Job matching: required check `name` is matched EXACTLY against the
 * job `name` (GitHub matrix jobs include the parenthesised variant, so
 * list the full name, e.g. "build (ubuntu-latest)"). When several jobs
 * share a name (re-runs, matrix), the LAST match in the run's job list
 * wins — it is the most recent attempt. A required entry may override
 * the matched job name with `jobName` when the protected check name
 * intentionally differs from the workflow job name.
 */

    if (typeof raw === 'string') {
        try { return JSON.parse(raw); } catch (e) { return raw; }
    }
    return raw;
}

/**
 * CI check-run mirroring for dispatch-only workflows.
 *
 * Problem: when a repository's CI is triggered via workflow_dispatch
 * (no pull_request trigger), GitHub does not associate the run's check
 * runs with open PRs — the branch-protection required checks stay
 * "expected/pending" forever, and the real pass/fail is invisible in
 * the PR Checks tab (a zombie check-run may exist on the head SHA from
 * a stale push event).
 *
 * Fix: re-read the ACTUAL jobs of the dispatch run and re-create one
 * check-run per required check name on the PR head SHA (same names,
 * same conclusions, summary links back to the source run). GitHub's
 * Checks UI and branch protection take the LATEST check-run per
 * (name, head SHA), so the mirror overrides any zombie.
 *
 * Tools used (dmtools registry, snake_case, synchronous):
 *   github_get_workflow_run_jobs({workspace, repository, runId})
 *       -> { total_count, jobs: [{id, name, status, conclusion, html_url}] }
 *   github_create_check_run({workspace, repository, name, headSha
 *       [, status][, title][, summary][, text]})
 *       -> check-run object (use .id for the follow-up update)
 *   github_update_check_run({workspace, repository, checkRunId,
 *       status, conclusion[, title][, summary][, text]})
 *   github_create_commit_status({workspace, repository, sha, state
 *       [, description][, context][, targetUrl]})
 *
 * Conclusion policy (documented behaviour of stampRequiredChecks):
 *   - job.conclusion === 'skipped'         -> NOT stamped (a skipped job
 *       must never green a required check); recorded in `skipped`.
 *   - job.status !== 'completed' (running/queued/null conclusion)
 *                                          -> NOT stamped; `skipped`
 *       entry with reason 'not-completed'.
 *   - success | neutral                    -> stamped as 'success' (and
 *       commit-status 'success' when the fallback is on).
 *   - failure | timed_out | startup_failure | cancelled | action_required
 *                                          -> stamped as-is ('cancelled'
 *       and 'action_required' map to commit-status 'failure' — GitHub
 *       statuses have no neutral value, and a cancelled CI run must not
 *       read as green on a PR).
 *
 * Job matching: required check `name` is matched EXACTLY against the
 * job `name` (GitHub matrix jobs include the parenthesised variant, so
 * list the full name, e.g. "build (ubuntu-latest)"). When several jobs
 * share a name (re-runs, matrix), the LAST match in the run's job list
 * wins — it is the most recent attempt. A required entry may override
 * the matched job name with `jobName` when the protected check name
 * intentionally differs from the workflow job name.
 */

function _parseJson(raw) {
    if (typeof raw === 'string') {
        try { return JSON.parse(raw); } catch (e) { return raw; }
    }
    return raw;
}

function _jobsOf(response) {
    var parsed = _parseJson(response);
    if (parsed && Array.isArray(parsed.jobs)) return parsed.jobs;

/**
 * CI check-run mirroring for dispatch-only workflows.
 *
 * Problem: when a repository's CI is triggered via workflow_dispatch
 * (no pull_request trigger), GitHub does not associate the run's check
 * runs with open PRs — the branch-protection required checks stay
 * "expected/pending" forever, and the real pass/fail is invisible in
 * the PR Checks tab (a zombie check-run may exist on the head SHA from
 * a stale push event).
 *
 * Fix: re-read the ACTUAL jobs of the dispatch run and re-create one
 * check-run per required check name on the PR head SHA (same names,
 * same conclusions, summary links back to the source run). GitHub's
 * Checks UI and branch protection take the LATEST check-run per
 * (name, head SHA), so the mirror overrides any zombie.
 *
 * Tools used (dmtools registry, snake_case, synchronous):
 *   github_get_workflow_run_jobs({workspace, repository, runId})
 *       -> { total_count, jobs: [{id, name, status, conclusion, html_url}] }
 *   github_create_check_run({workspace, repository, name, headSha
 *       [, status][, title][, summary][, text]})
 *       -> check-run object (use .id for the follow-up update)
 *   github_update_check_run({workspace, repository, checkRunId,
 *       status, conclusion[, title][, summary][, text]})
 *   github_create_commit_status({workspace, repository, sha, state
 *       [, description][, context][, targetUrl]})
 *
 * Conclusion policy (documented behaviour of stampRequiredChecks):
 *   - job.conclusion === 'skipped'         -> NOT stamped (a skipped job
 *       must never green a required check); recorded in `skipped`.
 *   - job.status !== 'completed' (running/queued/null conclusion)
 *                                          -> NOT stamped; `skipped`
 *       entry with reason 'not-completed'.
 *   - success | neutral                    -> stamped as 'success' (and
 *       commit-status 'success' when the fallback is on).
 *   - failure | timed_out | startup_failure | cancelled | action_required
 *                                          -> stamped as-is ('cancelled'
 *       and 'action_required' map to commit-status 'failure' — GitHub
 *       statuses have no neutral value, and a cancelled CI run must not
 *       read as green on a PR).
 *
 * Job matching: required check `name` is matched EXACTLY against the
 * job `name` (GitHub matrix jobs include the parenthesised variant, so
 * list the full name, e.g. "build (ubuntu-latest)"). When several jobs
 * share a name (re-runs, matrix), the LAST match in the run's job list
 * wins — it is the most recent attempt. A required entry may override
 * the matched job name with `jobName` when the protected check name
 * intentionally differs from the workflow job name.
 */

}

38:- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. 3:# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
4:# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
5-# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
6-#
7-#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
8-#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
9-#   asset        crap-baseline.json
10-#
11-# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
12:#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
13:#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.

/**
 * CI check-run mirroring for dispatch-only workflows.
 *
 * Problem: when a repository's CI is triggered via workflow_dispatch
 * (no pull_request trigger), GitHub does not associate the run's check
 * runs with open PRs — the branch-protection required checks stay
 * "expected/pending" forever, and the real pass/fail is invisible in
 * the PR Checks tab (a zombie check-run may exist on the head SHA from
 * a stale push event).
 *
 * Fix: re-read the ACTUAL jobs of the dispatch run and re-create one
 * check-run per required check name on the PR head SHA (same names,
 * same conclusions, summary links back to the source run). GitHub's
 * Checks UI and branch protection take the LATEST check-run per
 * (name, head SHA), so the mirror overrides any zombie.
 *
 * Tools used (dmtools registry, snake_case, synchronous):
 *   github_get_workflow_run_jobs({workspace, repository, runId})
 *       -> { total_count, jobs: [{id, name, status, conclusion, html_url}] }
 *   github_create_check_run({workspace, repository, name, headSha
 *       [, status][, title][, summary][, text]})
 *       -> check-run object (use .id for the follow-up update)
 *   github_update_check_run({workspace, repository, checkRunId,
 *       status, conclusion[, title][, summary][, text]})
 *   github_create_commit_status({workspace, repository, sha, state
 *       [, description][, context][, targetUrl]})
 *
 * Conclusion policy (documented behaviour of stampRequiredChecks):
 *   - job.conclusion === 'skipped'         -> NOT stamped (a skipped job
 *       must never green a required check); recorded in `skipped`.
 *   - job.status !== 'completed' (running/queued/null conclusion)
 *                                          -> NOT stamped; `skipped`
 *       entry with reason 'not-completed'.
 *   - success | neutral                    -> stamped as 'success' (and
 *       commit-status 'success' when the fallback is on).
 *   - failure | timed_out | startup_failure | cancelled | action_required
 *                                          -> stamped as-is ('cancelled'
 *       and 'action_required' map to commit-status 'failure' — GitHub
 *       statuses have no neutral value, and a cancelled CI run must not
 *       read as green on a PR).
 *
 * Job matching: required check `name` is matched EXACTLY against the
 * job `name` (GitHub matrix jobs include the parenthesised variant, so
 * list the full name, e.g. "build (ubuntu-latest)"). When several jobs
 * share a name (re-runs, matrix), the LAST match in the run's job list
 * wins — it is the most recent attempt. A required entry may override
 * the matched job name with `jobName` when the protected check name
 * intentionally differs from the workflow job name.
 */

function _parseJson(raw) {
    if (typeof raw === 'string') {
        try { return JSON.parse(raw); } catch (e) { return raw; }
    }
    return raw;
}

function _jobsOf(response) {
    var parsed = _parseJson(response);
    if (parsed && Array.isArray(parsed.jobs)) return parsed.jobs;

38:- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.

1:# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
2-#
3:# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
4:# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
5-# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
6-#
7-#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
8-#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
9-#   asset        crap-baseline.json
10-#
11-# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
12:#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
13:#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
14-# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
15-#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
16-#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
17-#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
18-#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.

38:- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. 1:# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
2-#
3:# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
4:# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
5-# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
6-#
7-#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
8-#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
9-#   asset        crap-baseline.json
10-#
11-# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
12:#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
13:#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
14-# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
15-#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
16-#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
17-#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
18-#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.

content.text:
## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

### Config composition
Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent

38:- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.

1:# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
2-#
3:# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
4:# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
5-# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
6-#
7-#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
8-#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
9-#   asset        crap-baseline.json
10-#
11-# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
12:#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
13:#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
14-# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
15-#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
16-#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
17-#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
18-#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.

blocks.text:
## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

### Config composition
Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent

1:# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
2-#
3:# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
4:# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
5-# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
6-#
7-#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
8-#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
9-#   asset        crap-baseline.json
10-#
11-# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
12:#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
13:#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
14-# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
15-#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
16-#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
17-#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
18-#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

### Config composition
Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent

38:- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) 1:# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
2-#
3:# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
4:# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
5-# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
6-#
7-#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
8-#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
9-#   asset        crap-baseline.json
10-#
11-# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
12:#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
13:#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
14-# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
15-#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
16-#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
17-#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
18-#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

### Config composition
Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent

38:- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative.
